nodes.name: In situ hydrothermal growth
nodes.procedure: FeMoO4 nanorods were in situ grown directly on nickel foam (FeMoO4/NF) via a facile hydrothermal process. The XRD pattern confirms mainly β-FeMoO4 phase (95 wt%) with small amount of α-FeMoO4 (5 wt%). SEM shows densely grown nanorods on NF surface. TEM reveals lattice fringes of 0.181 nm corresponding to (022) plane.
nodes.source_text: we report the development of an FeMoO4 nanorod array on nickel foam (FeMoO4/NF) via a facile hydrothermal process... FeMoO4 nanorods grown on nickel foam have been successfully synthesized via a facile hydrothermal process.

nodes.characterization_summary: The sample mainly comprises β-FeMoO4 phase with a small amount of α-FeMoO4. The mass fraction of β-FeMoO4 and α-FeMoO4 was 95:5 by XRD analysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of FeMoO4 scratched from NF. The diffraction peaks indicate that the sample mainly comprises a β-FeMoO4 phase with a small amount of α-FeMoO4 ... The mass fraction of β-FeMoO4 and α-FeMoO4 was 95:5 by XRD analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeMoO4 nanorods are densely grown on the entire surface of nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of FeMoO4/NF indicate that FeMoO4 nanorods are densely grown on the entire surface of nickel foam (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p binding energies at 724.1 eV (Fe 2p1/2) and 710.5 eV (Fe 2p3/2) for Fe2+; Mo 3d peaks at 235.5 eV (Mo 3d3/2) and 232.3 eV (Mo 3d5/2) for Mo6+; O 1s peaks at 530.4 eV (lattice oxygen) and 531.9 eV (chemisorbed oxygen).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectrum of FeMoO4 also confirms the presence of Fe, Mo, and O elements. For the Fe 2p spectrum (Fig. 2b), the binding energies at 724.1 and 710.5 eV for Fe2+ belong to Fe 2p1/2 and Fe 2p3/2, respectively... Fig. 2c shows the Mo 3d spectrum... peaks at 235.5 and 232.3 eV correspond to Mo 3d3/2 and Mo 3d5/2... The deconvolution of the O 1s peaks... reveals two components at 530.4 and 531.9 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of 1.62 mF cm^-2 from nonfaradaic CVs, indicating larger ECSA than powder/NF (0.64 mF cm^-2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl for FeMoO4 powder/NF and FeMoO4/NF are measured as 0.64 and 1.62 mF cm^-2 (Fig. 4c), respectively, indicating much larger surface areas and more exposed active sites for FeMoO4/NF.
